metadata.source: Torella, Raffaele: "The Svabodhodayamañjarī, or How to Suppress the Mind with No Effort". IN: R. Tsuchida and A. Wezler: Harānandalaharī. Studies in Honour of Prof. Minoru Hara on His Seventieth Birthday. Reinbeck : 2000, pp. 387-410.

children.translated_text: Through the investigation of right awakening (<s>samyagbodha</s>), [and] meditation on the absence of inherent nature,
I bow to the abode of the Self, [which has attained] the bliss of the dawn of awakening. (1)
This group of five beginning with form (<s>rūpa</s>) — the universe is just this much indeed;

children.text: gṛhyate pañcabhis tac ca cakṣurādibhir indriyaiḥ // 2 //
children.translated_text: and that is grasped by the five sense organs beginning with the eye. (2)

children.text: cakṣuḥ sarvāsv avasthāsu dehināṃ manasi sthitam /
children.translated_text: The eye, in all states of embodied beings, is established in the mind;

children.text: tat pralīnaṃ bhaved yasya tasya sarvaṃ pralīyate // 3 //
children.translated_text: for one in whom that [mind] becomes dissolved, everything dissolves. (3)
The method of its dissolution was taught by the <s>guru</s>s of old;
it has been made clear by me out of fear of the loss of that tradition. (4)
The conventional activity in the form of conceptual constructions such as birth and so on is established in the mind;

children.text: vastuto na tu tāḥ santi niścityaitac chamaṃ vrajet // 5 //
children.translated_text: but in reality they do not exist — having ascertained this, one should attain tranquility. (5)
At the time of the union of semen and blood, the mind does not exist anywhere;

children.text: na budbude na peṣyāṃ vā na śarīre kvacit sthitam // 6 //
children.translated_text: it is not in the bubble [of the early embryo], nor in the embryonic lump, nor established anywhere in the body. (6)
The body, within the womb-dwelling, in childhood, and likewise in youth,
is perishing every moment, ending in destruction — and that [mind] is never apprehended [in it]. (7)

children.text: pṛthag nāma pṛthag rūpaṃ lomādīnāṃ pṛthak sthitiḥ /
children.translated_text: The name is separate, the form is separate, the existence of hair and so on is separate;

children.text: pṛthak sarvaṃ yathā dṛṣṭaṃ kva śarīraṃ tadā sthitam // 8 //
children.translated_text: when everything is seen as separate, where then is the body established? (8)

children.text: evam eva vicāryoktā jātis tathaiva bādhyate /
children.translated_text: In the same way, birth, when investigated as described, is likewise refuted;

children.text: na ca sā vastuto yuktā kasyacid vāvabhāsate // 9 //
children.translated_text: and it is not logically established in reality, nor does it appear to anyone [as real]. (9)

children.text: nāma pitrā kṛtaṃ mithyā kriyā na niyatā yataḥ /
children.translated_text: The name given by the father is false, since action is not fixed;

children.text: guṇī yadi bhavet kaścid bhavanti bahavo guṇāḥ // 10 //
children.translated_text: if someone were a possessor of qualities, there would be many qualities [not one fixed nature]. (10)
Thus, overwhelmed by latent impressions (<s>vāsanā</s>s) arising from false conceptualization,
the restless nature of the mind — having ascertained this, one should bring about its cessation (<s>nirodha</s>). (11)
Cessation was taught by the ancients as accompanied by the yoga of detachment (<s>vairāgya</s>) and practice (<s>abhyāsa</s>);
this cessation is taught by us as [attainable] without effort. (12)

children.text: grāhyaṃ yac ca bhavet kiñcit tat tal līnaṃ tadā bhavet /
children.translated_text: Whatever graspable object there may be — when each of those has dissolved,
due to the non-grasping of anything else, the mind becomes quiescent in its own Self. (13)

children.text: yathā ghanasvane sāndre krameṇa vilayaṃ gate /
children.translated_text: Just as when a dense thunderous sound gradually goes to dissolution,
the mind, dependent on that support, becomes quiescent when it has faded. (14)

children.text: yad yan manoharaṃ kiṃcic chrutigocaram āgatam /
children.translated_text: Whatever captivating [sound] comes within the range of hearing,

children.text: ekāgraṃ bhāvayet tāvad yāval līnaṃ nirodhakṛt // 15 //
children.translated_text: one should meditate on it one-pointedly until it dissolves — [this] brings about cessation. (15)
Similarly, one should meditate in this way on the beauty of forms and so on;
afterward, nourished by the state of the Self, one should remember them as dissolved. (16)
Thus cessation has been taught by me through immersion in graspable objects;
[the method] prior to grasping itself is now demonstrated. (17)
One should awaken to the understanding that the sense organs here are [merely] instruments of grasping and are equal;
equanimity arises from the abandonment of attachment and likewise from the diminishing of aversion. (18)

children.text: sarvarāgāt sahāniḥ syāt sarvadveṣāt tathaiva ca /
children.translated_text: From attachment to all things there is harm, and likewise from aversion to all things;

children.text: baddhavat sarvarāgī syāt sarvadveṣṭā ca bhairavaḥ // 19 //
children.translated_text: one who is attached to everything would be like one bound, and one who hates everything [would be] terrible. (19)

children.text: agrāhyam indriyaṃ śūnyaṃ svātmany eva pralīyate /
children.translated_text: The sense organ, [being] ungraspable and empty, dissolves in its own Self;
and for one whose sense-activity has dissolved, there is the dawn of the arising of <s>kaivalya</s> (absolute freedom). (20)
Therefore, having placed the mind in the void, free from conceptualization,
when the activity of the senses has become still, cessation (<s>nirodha</s>) is born. (21)
For a <s>yogin</s> who is constantly yawning, or who is overtaken by hunger,

children.text: dhyāyato vā kim apy antaḥ pratyante kevalaṃ bhavet // 22 //
children.translated_text: or who is meditating on something within — at the culmination, the Absolute (<s>kevala</s>) may arise. (22)
For one whose mental activity has not [yet] dissolved, gradually taking recourse to sleep,
through the non-grasping of sense objects, complete cessation is born. (23)
For one who is running, through non-attention to the effort of stepping the feet,
when mental activity becomes free from conceptualization, the Supreme Self (<s>Paramātman</s>) shines forth. (24)

children.text: āsane 'py upaviṣṭasya kva me cittam avasthitam /
children.translated_text: Even for one seated on a seat, [inquiring] 'where is my mind established?'
by inquiring thus with effort, [the mind] becomes quiescent in the supportless. (25)
'By <s>vāyu</s> (wind/breath) I perform the movements and so on of the body' —

children.text: na ca citte sthito vāyur na vāyau cittam āsthitam // 26 //
children.translated_text: but the wind is not established in the mind, nor is the mind established in the wind. (26)

children.text: evaṃ vimṛśato bhāvān na kvacit saṃsthitaṃ manaḥ /
children.translated_text: For one thus examining the states of existence, the mind is not established anywhere;

children.text: mithaiva vṛttayas tasya sarvathā kevalaṃ sthitam // 27 //
children.translated_text: its activities are merely illusory — in every way, the Absolute (<s>kevala</s>) alone remains. (27)

children.text: yatra yatra bhaved vāñchā bhojanādiṣu vastuṣu /
children.translated_text: Wherever desire arises for objects such as food and so on,

children.text: pūrayet tām yathāśakti bhavet pūrṇo nirāśrayaḥ // 28 //
children.translated_text: one should fulfill it as far as possible — [then] one becomes full and without support [for further craving]. (28)

children.text: vāñchitaṃ gaditaṃ kiñcid akasmād yadi vismṛtam /
children.translated_text: If something desired and spoken about is suddenly forgotten,
from the renewed investigation of that [forgotten thought], one may attain <s>kaivalya</s> (absolute freedom) in an instant. (29)

children.text: sthānuḥ syāt puruṣo veti dūrād dṛśye vikalpite /
children.translated_text: 'Is that a post or a person?' — when something seen from afar is conceptualized thus,
for one of well-determined intellect, <s>nirodha</s> (cessation) quickly arises. // 30 //

children.text: dṛśyaiḥ padārthair draṣṭāraṃ paśyed buddhyā yato dṛśaḥ /
children.translated_text: Through visible objects one should see the seer (<s>draṣṭṛ</s>) with the intellect, since [he is the source] of seeing;

children.text: taṃ dṛṣṭvā mokṣam āpnoti yo na tadvat sa badhyate // 31 //
children.translated_text: having seen him, one attains <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation); whoever does not [see] thus is bound. // 31 //

children.text: ālambya saṃvidaṃ yatnāt saṃvedyaṃ na svabhāvataḥ /
children.translated_text: Resorting to awareness (<s>saṃvid</s>) with effort, the object of awareness is not [found] by its own nature;

children.text: tasmāt saṃviditaṃ sarvam iti saṃvinmayo bhavet // 32 //
children.translated_text: therefore, 'all is known'—thus one becomes pervaded by awareness (<s>saṃvinmaya</s>). // 32 //
Again, one should enter through the <s>apāna</s> (downward breath) and expand the heart;

children.text: tathaiva kṣīṇavṛttiḥ syād apāne vilayaṃ gate // 33 //
children.translated_text: thus, when the <s>apāna</s> has dissolved, one's mental activity (<s>vṛtti</s>) likewise becomes diminished. // 33 //
Resorting to the path of the <s>suṣumṇā</s> (central channel), through awareness of the resonance within the upper palace (<s>prāsāda</s>),
by abandoning the six <s>bindus</s> (energy-points), peaceful awakening (<s>śāntabodha</s>) arises in an instant. // 34 //
From the friction of the two <s>bindus</s> through the left and right movement,

great peace (<s>mahāśānti</s>) [arises] at the <s>dvādaśānta</s> (point twelve finger-breadths above)—so have the <s>siddhas</s> (perfected ones) declared in the oral tradition (<s>mukhāgama</s>). // 35 //

children.text: ūrdhvam ākramato vāyor udgatānte śamo bhavet /
children.translated_text: When the breath ascends upward, at the end of its rising, tranquility (<s>śama</s>) occurs;
even in the dissolution of the <s>puryaṣṭaka</s> (subtle body of eight constituents), likewise there is absorption (<s>laya</s>) of the mind. // 36 //
Having opened the mouth and remaining for a moment, without doubt, without agitation,
for one whose breath-activity (<s>prāṇavṛtti</s>) is arrested, <s>nirodha</s> (cessation) arises. // 37 //
Between the navel and the genitals, one should cast the mind at the end of sexual pleasure (<s>surata</s>);
when the bliss of love (<s>ratānanda</s>) is dissolving, one becomes waveless (<s>nistaraṅga</s>) for a moment. // 38 //
When one is attended by the embrace of a friend or relative who has come from afar—
the mind, filled to overflowing with bliss (<s>ānanda</s>), attains cessation (<s>nivṛtti</s>) in an instant. // 39 //
When a sound is uttered from afar, due to not grasping the meaning of the sound,
for one who is attentive, that knowledge arises with diminished obstruction. // 40 //
From massage and embrace of the feet, momentary cessation of the mind occurs. // 41 //
Upon the tip of the tongue, fix [your attention on] pleasant foods such as sweets (<s>ṣāḍava</s>);
when the bliss of taste (<s>rasānanda</s>) is diminishing, <s>kaivalya</s> (absolute liberation) arises. // 42 //
Likewise, one should contemplate the fragrances in <s>mālatī</s> (jasmine) and similar flowers;
by dependence on those [fragrances], when they dissolve, the mind dissolves [with them]. // 43 //

children.text: itthaṃ pratikṣaṇaṃ yasya cittam ātmani līyate /
children.translated_text: Thus, for one whose mind moment by moment dissolves into the <s>ātman</s> (Self),
he, having attained the true state of awakening, is called a <s>jīvanmukta</s> (one liberated while living). // 44 //
By <s>Vāmanadatta</s>, the son of <s>Harṣadatta</s>, the lion of the forest of <s>Mīmāṃsā</s>,
was composed the <s>Svabodhodayamañjarī</s> (A Bouquet of the Arising of Self-Awakening). // 45 //
